sre-bot: ALERT: realtime-api-eu p95/p99 anomaly detected (auto-detect). p95 from ~120ms -> ~520ms in last 5m; p99 from ~980ms -> ~3.2s. Streaming stall count ↑ 4x. paging: @Eric :rotating_light:
Eric: On it, taking pager. Can someone grab quick dashboard links and confirm customer impact?
Amanda: jumping in — Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/realtime/recent?panel=latency looks right. KV cache hit rate down ~30% on eu-region.
Jason: I see a small canary rollout finished ~3m ago on dedicated pool (hash-allocator v2). Could be related.
Devon: load graph shows traffic bump ~2.8x correlated w/ a marketing push at T-10m. But baseline p95 already elevated after the rollout.
Eric: ok - plan: 1) revert canary to previous config 2) route new sessions to dedicated fallback pool 3) enable prefix-cache fallback for streaming (temporary) 4) watch p95/p99. Who can run the route shift?
Amanda: I can flip route to fallback pool now. Doing `rbctl route set realtime-api-eu --pool=fallback-eu`
Amanda: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/hash-allocator -n realtime-canary` (started) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Jason: enabling prefix-cache fallback: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/configs/realtime/cache -d '{"prefix_fallback": true}'` — applying now.
Devon: adding short-term rate-limit on marketing IP range to reduce burst, pushed rule: `rl add --ip 34.122.5.0/24 --qps 100`
Eric: Revert finished, routing flip in progress, prefix fallback enabled. Watching.
Amanda: p95 down to ~210ms after flip, p99 ~1.1s. Streaming stall events reduced by ~60%.
Eric: good. Remaining gap likely due to cold KV misses while caches refill. Recommend warming strategy and follow-up: incremental prefetch and adjust ttl.
Lina: product note — two paying customers reported elevated latencies in last 20m via support. Not widespread but flagged. Will coordinate customer comms if we see further regression.
Jason: follow-up actions: 1) roll back canary until validated; 2) add a canary telemetry gate for kv-hit-rate < 85%; 3) run a replay on canary with synthetic traffic before re-enable.
Eric: oncall checklist: monitor p95/p99 dashboards, ensure alerts suppressed for noise, update incident doc. I'm staying on the page for next 30m.
Amanda: writing quick postmortem stub in incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/2845009999
Devon: note for eng-runtime: kernel selector on that build picks aggressive mem batching which may increase initial tail latency under burst — assigning to runtime team to review.
Eric: thanks all. If p95 creeps above 400ms again, we'll re-escalate. For now: mitigation successful, transition to post-incident review. :white_check_mark:
